questions.text:
Produce a piece of writing in te reo Māori (at least 150 words) on ONE of the following topics. Kuputaka/glossed vocabulary is provided to help but does not have to be included in your writing.

Topic 1: Whakatairitea ētahi runaruna e rua. Whakamāramatia mai ko tēhea te mea pai ake.
Compare and contrast two hobbies. Explain which is better.
Kuputaka: parakitihi = to practise/rehearse; pārekareka = to be fun; uaua = difficult; utu = cost; whakaohooho = to inspire

Topic 2: Matapakina mai tētahi raru i tō kura. He aha ētahi rautaki hei whakaea i tēnei raru?
Discuss a problem at your school. What are some solutions you can think of?
Kuputaka: kākahu = uniforms; kaupapa ako = subjects; nui = size; tawhito = old; tōkau = to be plain; whakaweti = bullying

Topic 3: Tuhia mai tētahi kōrero mō tētahi hui whakahirahira mō tō whānau. He aha te take koia nei te tino hui ki a koutou?
Write about an event that was significant for your whānau. Why was this event so important to you?
Kuputaka: aroha = love; koha = gift; mārena = wedding; whakaohooho = to inspire; whakapōtaetanga = graduation

Topic 4: Whakatairitea tō tino kai ki tētahi atu kai kāore e pai ki a koe. He aha ngā rerekētanga me ngā ōritenga?
Compare and contrast your favourite food with another food you don't like. What are the differences and similarities?
Kuputaka: kai whakauru = ingredients; kīnaki = sauce; reka = tastiness; rīhi = dishes; roa = length (of time); utu = cost

Topic 5: Ko wai te tangata rongonui e whiriwhiria e koe kia noho kōrua ki te kai tahi, ā, he aha te take i whiriwhiria e koe ko ia?
Which celebrity would you choose to have dinner with, and why did you choose them?
Kuputaka: angitū = success; kaiora = awesome, impressive; pūkenga = skilled in, skill(s); whakaohooho = to inspire; whakaute = to respect
questions.markingGuide:
This is a writing exam where you choose ONE topic and write at least 150 words in te reo Māori only.

Achieved (Paetae 3-4): Writes in te reo Māori on one of the topics. Writing is understandable and communication of ideas is mostly achieved. Shows sufficient basic evidence from Curriculum Levels 5 and 6. Contains errors but a few words in English for unknown translations are acceptable if infrequent. Simplistic ideas with few details or opinions.

Merit (Kaiaka 5-6): Writes in te reo Māori on one of the topics and adheres to the specific instructions. Writing is understandable with effective communication of ideas. Shows a range of complex evidence from Curriculum Levels 5 and 6. Contains few errors. Shows depth and regularly provides details and opinions.

Excellence (Kairangi 7-8): Comprehensive response in te reo Māori that shows a thorough understanding of the instructions. Communication of ideas is extensive. Shows a wide range of sophisticated evidence from Curriculum Levels 5 and 6. Contains minimal errors. Well-crafted response that is convincing; reasons and opinions are effectively placed and validate the candidate's ideas.
